messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automatic alert: sudden rise in 5xx + p99 latency on route /v1/generate detected at 4099990000. Current 5xx = 8.1% (baseline 0.4%), p99 latency 18.7s (baseline 0.9s). Canary deploy finished ~2m before spike. Notifying #incidents and oncall.

maya: ACK. I'm the oncall, pulling telemetry now. tagging @simon for runtime changes in the last deploy.

simon: looking. I merged a small change to kv-allocator + kernel selector in the canary that got promoted. Could be memory/eviction interaction with long-sequence requests.

maya: quick checks: tcp connection queues on routers? queue depth growth? cache thrash? leo can you check edge routing and proxy queues? 

leo: checking proxy metrics — connection backlog and keepalive look normal. I see router worker queues growing for a subset of hosts: hostset model-serving-2. Also saw a spike in TLS handshake wait times ~2m ago.

maya: running quick smoke:

```
curl -s -w "HTTP:%{http_code} T: %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | tee /tmp/smoke
cat /tmp/smoke
```
Response: multiple `HTTP:504 T: 30.001` from router IPs, backend returned connection timeout.

simon: logs from runtime indicate repeated stalls reading KV cache entries, threads blocked ~29s before returning 504. Stack shows `kv_cache::get` waiting on eviction lock.

maya: hypothesis: new kernel selector path introduced a contention case under certain seq len distributions, causing worker threads to block and backlog to propagate to routers -> 504/timeouts. Agrees with post-deploy timing.

carla: how many customers affected? any high-traffic tenants hit hard? we need a customer impact blurb for comms.

maya: preliminary: about 12% of in-flight requests across /v1/generate; top 3 customers seeing spike in error rates to ~25-30% in last 5m. Notifying CS. Marking SEV2 until rollback confirmed.

simon: I recommend immediate rollback of the canary promotion to stop further exposure and restore baseline. Change is small but risky. Can we revert and confirm? 

maya: authorize rollback. deploy-bot, can you initiate rollback of last promotion to stable? include note: hot rollback for late-token stall.

deploy-bot: Rollback command issued: `redwoodctl rollout undo stable --from=canary --reason="post-deploy p99 spike - late token stall"`.

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: 20% -> 60% -> 100%. All stable replicas back to previous image. Health checks green. :white_check_mark:

maya: after rollback metrics: 5xx dropped from 8.1% -> 0.6% in ~45s, p99 down from 18.7s -> 0.95s. Good signal. Confirming with smoke tests.

maya: smoke curl now returns `HTTP:200 T: 0.73` consistently across routers.

carla: thanks. I'll open an incident ticket and update affected customers: "We experienced elevated timeouts and errors on /v1/generate shortly after a recent deploy. We rolled back and service is restored. Investigating root cause."

simon: collecting runtime traces and heap/lock profiles from the failing revision for postmortem. I'll grab profiles from the canary infra (retained for 1h). Anyone saw anything in MD logs about `kv_eviction` churn? 

leo: yes, agent logs show eviction thrash spikes coincident with GC cycles on the canary instances. I'll attach router-level packet drops and queue lengths to the ticket.

maya: immediate mitigation: rollback done, traffic normalized. Escalate to postmortem owner @simon. Oncall handoff in 30m to next SRE. 

carla: customer comm draft saved to incident ticket. CS to send targeted notes to top affected accounts with incident summary and ETA for RCA.

simon: postmortem items: 1) reproduce with synthetic workload (long sequences + high concurrency) 2) add lock contention telemetry & knob to disable new selector quickly 3) safer rollout gating for kernel selector changes 4) add canary traffic shape tests.

maya: adding runbook item: if p95/p99 > 3s after deploy and 5xx > 1% for 2 consecutive minutes, trigger automated rollback and notify oncall.

leo: created grafana panel and alert tweak PR: #4256, linking to incident.

deploy-bot: Note: rollback generated a change id 2026-409999-rollback, recorded in deploy audit log.

maya: handing incident to simon for deep dive and RCA. I'll stay available for follow-ups. Oncall transfer to next shift in 28m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

simon: ack, taking postmortem ownership. Will schedule a 1-hour RCA and invite eng-runtime, infra, and product. Thanks team.

carla: tagging customer success for follow-up and postmortem notes. Closing immediate paging loop — service stable. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident closed (service restored) at 4099990261. Metrics returning to baseline.
